result.summary: This draft PR adds a new bitcoin-tidy check ('combine-assignments') that detects consecutive assignments to annotated struct members and suggests replacing them with a constructor call. It applies the check to COutPoint, CTxIn, and CTxOut by adding CONSTRUCTOR_ARGUMENT annotations and mechanically rewriting ~40 files (mostly tests and benches) to use constructor calls instead of piecewise field assignment. The stated goal is to demonstrate that most mutation of these primitives happens in test code, as groundwork for eventually making them immutable.
result.problem: Validation code does not require COutPoint/CTxOut/CTxIn to be mutable; that requirement comes from test code written in a procedural rather than declarative style, per issue #35904's discussion of a stateless validation library. This PR is exploratory tooling meant to quantify and mechanically fix that mutation, mainly benefiting maintainers pursuing the immutability/encapsulation project (also touched by #35569).

open_concerns: maflcko asked whether the CONSTRUCTOR_ARGUMENT annotation is even necessary versus clang-tidy deriving constructor args itself, to avoid a second source of truth (unanswered in code, discussed only conceptually).

maflcko questioned whether extending the immutability effort beyond CTransaction to COutPoint/CTxOut/CTxIn is worth the churn, given #35569 (the related encapsulation PR) is already somewhat controversial.
alexanderwiederin flagged a possible witness-drop regression in test/util/transaction_utils.cpp; author confirmed it does drop the witness but no fix has landed since.
maflcko's 2026-08-24 suggestion to use init-list syntax (referencing #36019) is unanswered.

The author and janb84 discussed three different paths forward (merge as-is, do it class-by-class ending in immutability, or use the tool only as a backlog/never merge the annotations); the author now leans toward the third, meaning this PR's own annotations may never be merged.
resolved_concerns: maflcko's narrowing-conversion comment on ccoins_caching.cpp was discussed; author explained aggregate initialization doesn't compile everywhere, and maflcko said he had no strong opinion and would be happy to review a follow-up.
The check's naming ('bitcoin-tidy' name was confusing) was raised by maflcko with a rename suggestion; not clearly implemented but treated as a nit.

result.card: Draft PR adding a bitcoin-tidy 'combine-assignments' linter and mechanically rewriting ~40 mostly test/bench files to build COutPoint/CTxIn/CTxOut via constructors instead of piecewise field assignment, as a proof of concept for eventually making these primitives immutable (referencing issue #35904 on a stateless validation library and related PR #35569). Several reviewers gave concept ACKs (l0rinc, josibake, alexanderwiederin), but maflcko questioned whether extending immutability beyond CTransaction is worth the churn, and the author himself now leans toward never merging these annotations, instead using the tool only to find candidate files for manual rewrites. The PR is currently unreviewable as-is: CI is failing, it needs rebase, and the author has been silent since 2026-08-21 with an open maintainer question about init-list syntax from 2026-08-24. Its main lasting value would be as a design discussion catalyst and dev-tooling addition rather than a behavior change, since the diff touches no validation, mempool, or RPC semantics directly.
